influences.name: Jim O'Rourke
influences.context: the third era is one that die-hards appreciate, but are still trying to reckon with. Rather Ripped moves away from all three stages. It is a big, fat, pogo-stick-of-a bounce from its siblings in the Trilogy, which were largely influenced by Jim O'Rourke's temporary stint in the band.

influences.name: Iggy Pop
influences.context: Well, maybe when Iggy sang one of our songs in London and we were there.

influences.name: The Rolling Stones
influences.context: You guys are influential. Is there any one particular band that you're most proud of influencing? Moore: Oh, um, maybe The Stones.

influences.name: Paul McCartney
influences.context: Yeah, hanging out with McCartney. He watched us from the side of the stage during an acoustic set, and came up afterwards wanting to know all about our tunings and stuff. We got his blessing and that was great. People like that, with that much history… it's validating.

influences.context: named after a book by Jack Kerouac, who is Ranaldo's favourite writer

influences.name: Sylvia Plath

influences.name: Glenn Branca
influences.context: Thurston Moore and Lee Ranaldo found themselves in the immediate orbit of a composer who built their entire career around the energy of New York's chaotic decay, Glenn Branca... Early iterations of Branca's 'guitar orchestra' became home to Moore and Ranaldo, who would use Branca's techniques — like playing guitars with power-tools — and ethos as an essential basis for the founding of Sonic Youth.

influences.name: John Cage
influences.context: No Wave was characterized by its opposition to everything happening around it, especially western song-structure and tonality. The result was a panoply of abrasive sounds, and chaotic flirtations with performance art which made forerunners like John Cage appear comparably conservative.

influences.name: Mike Kelley
influences.context: One such artist was the late Mike Kelley — an artist Kim Gordon had befriended during her art school days in L.A. (via SonicYouth.com)... Kelley worked with Sonic Youth and its members on and off throughout his career.

influences.name: Hard Core and No Wave
influences.context: Thurston Moore says they were inspired by the do it yourself energy of Hard Core and No Wave.

influences.name: Glen Broncha
influences.context: The band's other guitarist, Lee Ranaldo, had played in composer Glen Broncha's guitar orchestra and like Broncha, Ranaldo says Sonic Youth employed unusual tunings to get the sounds it wanted.

influences.name: The Kingsmen
influences.context: I was five or six when I heard this; it was my older brother's single. The sound of the electric guitar was the most magnificent thing. Also, the idea of a band was so exciting.

influences.name: Brian Eno
influences.context: The magic of the lyrics meant so much to me as a teenager. Later, I read Eno had just put the words together to sound good, that they didn't make sense. I felt really let down at first, but he created real adventure in language and I'm OK with that now!

influences.name: Ramones
influences.context: They made music on such minimalist lines at the same time as the classical minimalists and were so high concept, while also being post-Gary Glitter glam. They remind you how literate really direct music can be.

influences.name: Dinosaur Jr
influences.context: To hear a musician who'd come out of US hardcore and Oi!, and not be afraid to play great guitar histrionics and be heartfelt in songwriting, at that point of my career in Sonic Youth, really astounded me.

influences.name: Solange
influences.context: I've just travelled from the west to east coast of America with my 22-year-old daughter and this played all the way. Rock's not experimental in the mainstream these days, maybe because it comes from a place of privilege. R&B really is.

influences.name: Chögyam Trungpa
influences.context: I've been teaching poetry in summer schools at Naropa University in Colorado, founded by the Tibetan Buddhist Chögyam Trungpa, a close associate of the monk who told David Bowie in the 60s to do music rather than join a monastery. Much of the teaching there is about consciousness
